sec: TFT patterns: thyrotoxicosis, T3-toxicosis, sick-euthyroid, thyroglobulin

items.q: Match the printed biochemical pattern — 1) Thyrotoxicosis 2) T3-toxicosis 3) Sick-euthyroid (page schematic) 4) ↓TBG (cirrhosis) … A) ↓TSH, normal T4, ↑FT4, normal T3, ↑FT3 B) ↓TSH, normal T4, normal FT4, normal T3, ↑FT3 C) Normal totals, ↑rT3, ↓FT3 D) Normal totals, ↓TBG
items.exp: The schematic prints thyrotoxicosis as ↓TSH with normal T4 but raised FT4 and normal T3 with raised FT3; T3-toxicosis raises only FT3; sick-euthyroid leaves totals normal with rT3 high and FT3 low; cirrhosis drops TBG without changing free hormone. (Book p904)

items.q: A patient has suppressed TSH with normal total T4 and total T3 but elevated free T3. The most consistent label is:
items.exp: Isolated free-T3 elevation with otherwise normal totals fits the page's T3-toxicosis pattern. (Book p904)

items.q: Assess the source's totals/free schematic: I Thyrotoxicosis row shows FT4 and FT3 both elevated. II Sick-euthyroid row prints normal total hormone values.
items.exp: The thyrotoxicosis row has both FT4 and FT3 raised; the sick-euthyroid row keeps totals normal with FT3 low. (Book p904)

items.q: Match the following state to its TBG / binding-protein print on the page — 1) Pregnancy 2) Cirrhosis 3) Familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia … A) ↑TBG B) ↓TBG C) Albumin binds excess T4, raising total T4 with normal free hormone
items.exp: Pregnancy raises TBG; cirrhosis lowers TBG; FDHS binds excess T4 to albumin raising total T4 with normal free hormone. (Book p904)

items.q: A patient with cirrhosis has normal free T4, normal TSH, low TBG and low total T4. The free-hormone result correctly classifies the patient as:
items.exp: Cirrhosis lowers TBG and therefore total T4, but free T4 and TSH are preserved — the patient is euthyroid. (Book p904)

items.q: Thyroglobulin is ___ in every cause of hyperthyroidism except ___, where it is low.
items.exp: The page lists thyroglobulin as raised in all causes of thyrotoxicosis except factitious ingestion, where it is low. (Book p904)

items.q: Assess the source's thyroglobulin teaching: I Thyroglobulin is raised in subacute thyroiditis. II Thyroglobulin is raised in factitious thyrotoxicosis.
items.exp: Subacute thyroiditis releases stored thyroglobulin, raising it; factitious intake of exogenous hormone suppresses thyroid activity so thyroglobulin is low. (Book p904)

items.q: Match the following pattern to the expected free hormone on the page — 1) Subclinical hyperthyroidism 2) T3-toxicosis 3) FDHS 4) Factitious thyrotoxicosis … A) Normal FT4, normal FT3, ↓TSH B) Normal FT4, ↑FT3, ↓TSH C) ↑Total T4, normal free hormone, normal TSH D) ↑FT4, ↓TSH, low thyroglobulin
items.exp: Subclinical hyperthyroidism has normal free hormones with low TSH; T3-toxicosis raises only free T3; FDHS raises only total T4; factitious raises free T4 with low thyroglobulin. (Book p904)

items.q: An over-the-counter 'thyroid support' user has suppressed TSH, raised free T4 and a low thyroglobulin. Which diagnostic label fits?
items.exp: Factitious intake suppresses endogenous thyroid activity and therefore thyroglobulin, while exogenous T4 raises free T4. (Book p904)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a state where thyroglobulin is raised?
items.exp: Factitious thyrotoxicosis is the only cause on the page where thyroglobulin is low; the others raise thyroglobulin. (Book p904)

items.q: In the page's sick-euthyroid arrow schematic, which direction does the FT3 arrow point?
items.exp: The schematic draws FT3 down as part of the low-T3 / high-rT3 pattern of non-thyroidal illness. (Book p904)

items.q: In familial dysalbuminaemic hyperthyroxinaemia, total T4 is ___ while free T4 and TSH remain ___.
items.exp: Albumin-binding variants raise total T4 but free T4 and TSH are preserved; FDHS mimics true hyperthyroidism only on total assays. (Book p904)

items.q: Assess this sick-euthyroid note: I The schematic marks rT3 as up. II The schematic marks FT3 as up.
items.exp: Reverse T3 is marked up while free T3 is marked down, reflecting impaired T4-to-T3 activation and dominant D3 in critical illness. (Book p904)

items.q: Match the following thyrotoxicosis pattern to its free-hormone print — 1) Graves disease 2) Subacute thyroiditis 3) Toxic adenoma 4) Struma ovarii … A) ↑FT4 and ↑FT3 B) ↑FT4 with low thyroglobulin only in factitious C) ↑FT4/FT3 from ectopic thyroid tissue D) Transient ↑FT4 with raised thyroglobulin and ESR
items.exp: Graves and toxic adenoma raise both FT4 and FT3; subacute thyroiditis causes a transient rise with raised thyroglobulin and ESR; struma ovarii produces ectopic thyroid hormone secretion. (Book p904)
